# RemoteAssetSource

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.SceneBuilding` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/SceneBuilder/AssetSources/RemoteAssetSource.cs#L41)

Reads an external asset database described by a JSON manifest and imports its assets on
demand. Point [`remoteManifestUrl`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-scenebuilding/SceneBuilderSettings#remotemanifesturl) at an endpoint serving:

```csharp
{
  "version": 1,
  "assets": [
    {
      "id":          "unique-stable-id",
      "name":        "Office Chair",
      "description": "Swivel chair, 4k textures",
      "category":    "Models",
      "tags":        ["furniture", "office"],
      "thumbnailUrl":"https://.../chair.png",
      "downloadUrl": "https://.../chair.fbx",
      "author":      "CIE Group",
      "version":     "1.2",
      "sizeBytes":   1048576
    }
  ]
}
```

"category" is free text used for grouping. Use the [`AssetCategories`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-scenebuilding/AssetCategories) names -
Models, Sounds, Textures - for entries that should behave like the built-in ones; the
browser is scoped to those three kinds of content.
The manifest is cached under Library/ so opening the window does not hit the network every
time, and downloaded files land in [`remoteDownloadFolder`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-scenebuilding/SceneBuilderSettings#remotedownloadfolder).
With no URL configured the source reports itself unconfigured and stays out of the way.

```csharp
public class RemoteAssetSource : IAssetSource
```
